title: Measures of spread: range, variance and standard deviation

videos.script: Lia and Davi both deliver for Horta. Over eight deliveries each, both average exactly thirty-five minutes. {{both}} By the mean, they are the same courier. Now look at the times. {{times}} Lia's deliveries take between thirty-three and thirty-six minutes. Every one of them. You could set a clock by her. {{lia}} Davi's take anything from twenty-two to forty-four. Some customers get their shopping in record time. Others wait three quarters of an hour and phone to complain. {{davi}} The mean cannot see the difference, because the fast deliveries and the slow ones cancel out. To see it, you need a second number: how far the values tend to sit from the centre. {{spread}} This lesson builds that number in three steps. The range first, which is easy and fragile. Then the variance, which squares the distances. Then the standard deviation, which brings them back to minutes. {{steps}} By the end you will compute Davi's standard deviation by hand, and you will know why the formula divides by seven and not by eight. {{seven}}
